label: prf:transfer-matrix-level-independence
html:
Proof.

(1) Constituent-composite agreement. By (constituent-composite agreement), the constituent product \prod \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}} equals the composite Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q) as exact elements of H_N(q).

(2) Path independence on \mathcal{S}_p. All braiding takes place within the exceptional divisor (vertex operators factor through \mathcal{S}_p). Two braiding operations T_1, T_2 that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have braid words \beta_1, \beta_2 whose closures \hat{\beta}_1, \hat{\beta}_2 are ambient-isotopic. By the link invariance of the Markov trace (Jones--Markov trace, property 3), \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_1)) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_2)). Hence \hat{V}(T_1) = \hat{V}(T_2) and \mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2).

The specific sequence of crossings within \mathcal{S}_p does not matter: all that matters is the isotopy class of the resulting link. The blow-down map \pi collapses \mathcal{S}_p to p, erasing the internal history.

(3) Well-definedness. Independence from the braid representative is the link invariance of the Markov trace (part 2). Independence from the PawLei embedding follows from the q-Schur--Weyl duality: any two embeddings \iota, \iota' of V_{j_i} into V^{\otimes 2j_i} differ by an element of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra centralizer, which commutes with the Markov trace. Independence from the order of crossing evaluation follows from the right-to-left peeling argument in the Markov trace product (Markov trace product): the generators are peeled in decreasing order, and the result is independent of the order in which crossings at a fixed generator were originally applied. \square
